biography: Dale Wood, a name synonymous with aggressive late-braking maneuvers and a never-say-die attitude in the Australian motorsport scene, hails from the dusty outback town of Broken Hill. His racing journey began, not on asphalt, but on the sun-baked dirt tracks of his family's sheep station, tearing around in a beat-up ute. A chance encounter with a visiting Supercars team during a promotional event ignited his passion, convincing him to trade sheep shearing for gear shifts. Wood clawed his way through the ranks, starting in Formula Ford before making the leap to Supercars. A defining moment came at Bathurst in 2018, when, driving for a smaller team, he held off a charging Craig Lowndes for ten nail-biting laps. Now in his peak years with Edge Motorsports, Wood is a consistent contender, hungry for championship glory and unafraid to ruffle feathers to get there.
drivingStyle: Wood's driving style is characterized by raw aggression and a relentless pursuit of every tenth of a second. He's known for his late-braking overtakes, often pushing the limits of adhesion and leaving rivals scrambling for space. While some criticize his sometimes overly-aggressive approach, his tire management is surprisingly good, a skill honed from years of racing on abrasive surfaces. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest, a testament to his mental fortitude and competitive spirit.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at Phillip Island in 2020, where Rossi accused Wood of intentionally wrecking him.
A fierce on-track rivalry due to their similar aggressive driving styles, leading to frequent close calls and heated battles for position.
Nakamura's clinical and calculated driving style clashes with Wood's more impulsive approach, creating tension and a constant battle for track dominance.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, despite their questionable hygiene.
Listens to AC/DC at full volume in the garage before every race.
Has a habit of meticulously cleaning his helmet visor, even when it's already spotless.
famousQuote: You gotta be a bit of a mongrel out there. Nice guys finish last.
careerHighlight: Winning the Bathurst 1000 in 2022 with Edge Motorsports, a stunning victory that cemented his place as one of Australia's top drivers after a hard fought race. He and his co-driver had a stellar performance, gaining positions on pit strategy and late race overtakes.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Adelaide 500 in 2019, a heartbreaking moment that cost him a guaranteed victory and left him questioning his own judgement.
